question: What is another widely recognized medical name for leprosy?
explanation: Leprosy is named Hansen's disease after Gerhard Armauer Hansen, the Norwegian physician who identified the causative organism. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which body systems are primarily affected by leprosy?
explanation: The causative bacterium has a unique tropism for cooler body tissues, specifically infecting the peripheral nerves and cutaneous layers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h1)

question: What type of organism causes leprosy?
explanation: Mycobacterium leprae retains certain stains even after acid wash, classifying it as an acid-fast bacillus similar to the tuberculosis bacterium. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h2)

question: How is leprosy primarily transmitted between individuals?

options.A: Ingestion of contaminated municipal water supplies
options.B: Direct penetration of unbroken skin by soil larvae
options.D: Prolonged close contact with respiratory droplets

explanation: Infection spreads through repeated household exposure to nasal secretions and droplet spread from untreated infected persons over a long period. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h2)

question: A patient presenting with more than five skin lesions is categorized under which operational type?
explanation: The operational cutoff for multibacillary classification is six or more skin lesions or nerve involvement exceeding one nerve trunk. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h3)

question: What immunological feature distinguishes the tuberculoid end of the leprosy spectrum from the lepromatous end?

options.A: Enhanced ability of macrophages to lyse red cells
options.C: Massive proliferation of bacilli in the blood

explanation: Tuberculoid leprosy patients mount a robust cell-mediated immune response that successfully localizes and restricts the multiplication of the bacteria. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the hallmark sensory finding in a suspected leprosy skin lesion?

options.B: Loss of sensation to pain and temperature
options.C: Hyperalgesia when exposed to cold water

explanation: Cutaneous nerve destruction in leprosy lesions leads to a characteristic impairment or total loss of thermal and pain perception. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h4)

question: A patient presents with an asymmetrical skin patch on the forearm that lacks sensation. Which peripheral nerve should the nurse palpate first to check for localized enlargement?
explanation: The ulnar nerve is a superficial peripheral nerve frequently assessed for thickening and tenderness in upper limb involvement. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do patients with advanced leprosy frequently develop severe foot ulcers without noticing early tissue injury?

options.A: Loss of protective pain and pressure sensations in the extremities
options.B: Systemic deposition of immune complexes in foot joints
options.C: Complete destruction of bone matrix by direct bacterial invasion
options.D: Rapid ischemic necrosis caused by total arterial occlusion

explanation: Because peripheral neuropathy eliminates pain feedback, patients continue walking on injured or pressured tissue, causing painless chronic wounds. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which eye complication is commonly associated with facial nerve damage in leprosy?
explanation: Weakness of the orbicularis oculi muscle leads to incomplete eyelid closure, exposing the cornea to drying and trauma. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is monotherapy avoided when treating leprosy?

options.D: It neutralizes the body's natural flora

explanation: Using a single anti-leprosy drug leads to fast bacterial mutation and treatment failure, making combination therapy mandatory. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary operational purpose of Multi-Drug Therapy in community settings?

options.A: To stimulate rapid regeneration of destroyed skin pigment
options.B: To cure the infection and eliminate sources of transmission
options.C: To immediately reverse existing fixed nerve deformities
options.D: To provide permanent immunity against future reinfection

explanation: MDT clears viable bacilli from the body, rapidly rendering the patient non-contagious and curing the disease. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary rationale for teaching daily self-inspection of hands and feet to a patient with nerve damage?

options.A: To measure the exact reduction in skin fold thickness over time
options.B: To detect early micro-injuries before severe ulceration develops
options.C: To assess whether systemic pigmentation is returning to normal
options.D: To monitor the daily growth rate of cutaneous bacterial colonies

explanation: Daily checking compensates for lost pain sensation, allowing patients to spot blisters or minor cuts and treat them before they become infected ulcers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which intervention is most appropriate when managing dry, anesthetic skin on a patient's foot?

options.A: Exposing the foot to direct sunlight to stimulate blood flow
options.B: Soaking in water followed by applying protective oil or cream
options.C: Applying strong antiseptic ointments without prior washing
options.D: Scrubbing vigorously with a stiff brush to remove dead tissue

explanation: Hydrating the skin through soaking and locking in moisture with emollients prevents cracking and subsequent bacterial entry. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is a major advantage of integrating leprosy diagnosis and treatment into general primary health care clinics?

options.A: It completely prevents the occurrence of immune-mediated reactions
options.B: It reduces social stigma and encourages early health-seeking behavior
options.C: It eliminates the need for multi-drug therapy drug combinations
options.D: It shortens the standard incubation period of the bacterial infection

explanation: Treating leprosy alongside general illnesses removes the fear of isolation linked to specialized clinics, prompting patients to report symptoms sooner. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h8)

question: Which strategy is essential for breaking the chain of transmission within an affected community?

options.A: Mandatory surgical removal of all thickened peripheral nerves
options.B: Quarantining all diagnosed families in isolated camps
options.C: Active case finding and screening of household contacts
options.D: Mass administration of prophylactic vaccines to healthy adults

explanation: Identifying hidden cases early and screening close household contacts ensures prompt treatment, halting further spread in the population. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h8)
